question: Does the two-possible-commanded-target inference and single missing-ACK target-history divergence persist for genuinely different ManiSkill robot bodies, Panda and xArm6, with separately configured native target pose controllers?
source: mani-skill/ManiSkill official PickCube-v1 and independent robot kinematics/URDF; no new policy trained or transferred
actuator_behavior: native controller, actual separate PhysX environments

truths: native ZERO arm delta delivered instead
intervention.gripper: zero fixed in all paired worlds

scripted_actions: deterministic bounded 6D native translation/rotation action at t0,t1,t2 using only action index, with a nontrivial t2 delta; all other steps are zero. Same native commands for both robots, but metric displacement depends on each robot's separately configured gain.
measures: same robot applied-v-held real target XYZ and angle separation after fault
two native action-history predicted target poses vs actual branch-specific private target pose (audit only AFTER physx step)
achieved_EE_probe_response distance between both real faults
condition number/zero-history-indistinguishability if target separation is zero
hypothesis: Known action history plus known native controller chart predicts each possible commanded target on both robot implementations; missing delivery ACK causes nonzero hypothesized target divergence even under identical messages. This does NOT establish that active proprioception can distinguish those histories, or that any frozen Panda PPO transfers to xArm6.
failure_policy: Any missing robot asset, unsupported controller chart or runtime incompatibility results in explicit failure, no fallback to Panda substitute. Keep negative outcome even when xArm6 IK fails.
gates: Eight successful original shard PhysX execution if sharded
actual separate xArm6 native URDF and articulation
no private target getter in history observer
private getter permitted for postphysical audit only
raw per-robot individual errors and probes
no model training or Panda PPO insertion
